source_document.body:
Trans-Pacific ocean rates remain well above pre-peak levels, and carriers are seeking increases of $2,000–$3,000 per FEU for November despite signs that the prolonged peak season is ending.
Forwarders cited improving space availability and more consistent vessel schedules as reasons to doubt that the increases would stick, analyst and SONAR data contributor Freightos (NASDAQ: CRGO ) said in an update.
The analyst pegged Asia–U.S. East Coast rates at about $9,900/FEU, down 6% from the previous week but still roughly $200 above their level two weeks earlier. West Coast rates remained near $8,300/FEU after climbing into that range in September.
A potential watchmen’s strike at Los Angeles and Long Beach adds another source of uncertainty.
The Pacific Maritime Association and International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 26 extended their agreement through 5 p.m. Pacific Time on November 4, postponing a possible November 1 walkout while negotiations continue with federal mediation. The watchmen’s previous contract expired in July 2025.
Sources told FreightWaves that negotiations are continuing as of Wednesday.
Local 26 represents approximately 250 workers who provide terminal security services. Despite its small membership, a strike could have a wider operational impact. According to the Pacific Maritime Association, the affected facilities handle roughly 85% of Long Beach cargo and 33% of Los Angeles cargo. Employers have also warned that other ILWU members could honor picket lines, potentially interrupting vessel, yard and gate operations.
Container shipping rates from Asia to Europe have risen over the past month despite expectations of weaker post-peak demand and a growing return to Red Sea routes.
Rates to Northern Europe have climbed 10% over the past month, while Mediterranean prices have gained 23%. The increases come as congestion and lingering cargo backlogs help support prices, and uncertainty as to whether demand will sustain another round of hikes.
Mediterranean rates rose 3% last week to $4,375 per FEU, while Northern Europe prices were broadly unchanged at $3,595/FEU.
Congestion at Northern European hubs and lingering backlogs in the Far East may be contributing to upward pressure. A coordinated labor action on Oct. 30 also threatened disruption across European and other ports. More than 25 unions organized strikes and demonstrations at 113 ports across 22 countries and territories, although the impact varied, with some locations holding demonstrations rather than stopping cargo operations.
The rate gains have coincided with an accelerating return to the shorter Suez Canal-Red Sea route. Premier Alliance is adding two Asia–Mediterranean services to its Suez network in November, following earlier decisions to restore other services through the Red Sea. The shift is beginning to release vessels previously needed to maintain longer, diverted sailings around Africa, although congestion continues to absorb capacity on Asia–Northern Europe services.
Carriers planned general rate increases, or GRIs, of $1,000–$1,500/FEU on Asia–Europe lanes at the start of November, according to the update, with further increases planned for mid-month. Daily rates were flat in the opening days of the week, leaving the success of those efforts uncertain.
But published reports found carriers were discounting early-November bookings even as they announced higher rates, with Linerlytica describing the November 1 Asia–Northern Europe increase as “effectively doomed.” Carriers are also seeking stronger spot prices during the annual contract tendering season, when those prices help guide negotiations.
The two major east–west trades have followed different paths. Asia–Europe prices fell by $2,000–$3,000/FEU between July and September, returning close to their mid-May, pre-peak baseline before recovering in October. Trans-Pacific prices, by contrast, remain about $5,500/FEU above their pre-peak levels, the analyst said.
That resilience, including after China’s Golden Week holiday, leaves a relatively short window for a substantial correction before demand is expected to strengthen ahead of Lunar New Year. A return to pre-peak trans-Pacific pricing before the next seasonal upswing therefore remains uncertain.
Why it matters: Importers face high shipping costs and uncertain delivery times despite cooling demand, complicating budgets and inventory planning. A port strike could add delays and further limit relief.

Heavier shipments are driving higher tonnage and revenue per bill at ArcBest’s less-than-truckload unit. Freight lost to a once-depressed truckload market is returning alongside an improved manufacturing complex. The changing freight mix helped the company beat third-quarter expectations on Wednesday.
The Institute for Supply Management’s Manufacturing PMI remained in expansion territory for a 10th consecutive month in October. The 55.5 reading was 100 basis points above expectations and the September mark. (A reading above 50 signals expansion, while one below 50 indicates contraction.)
ArcBest ( NASDAQ: ARCB ) reported adjusted earnings per share of $2.62 on Wednesday before the market opened. The result was 79% higher year over year and 11 cents better than the consensus estimate. (The adjusted number excluded restructuring, technology and other nonrecurring costs.)
Consolidated revenue was up 15% y/y to $1.21 billion, in line with consensus.
Table: ArcBest’s key performance indicators
LTL: Q3 by the numbers
The company’s asset-based unit, which includes LTL subsidiary ABF Freight, reported revenue of $799 million, a 10% y/y increase. Tonnage was up 10% y/y as shipments declined 3% and weight per shipment jumped 13%. On a y/y comparison, tonnage increased 8.1% in July, 9.1% in August and 11.6% in September.
Revenue per hundredweight was 1% higher y/y (inclusive of fuel surcharges) and revenue per shipment was 14% higher, with both metrics being impacted by the higher shipment weights. Excluding fuel, yield dropped by a low single-digit percentage in the period, dragged down by heavier shipment weights and a 2% shorter average length of haul.
Contractual rate increases averaged 5.1% in the quarter (up 9.6% on a two-year-stacked comparison). ArcBest implemented a 5.9% general rate increase for LTL services in both of its business units in June.
A 90.4% adjusted operating ratio (inverse of operating margin ) was 210 bps better y/y. The result was 40 bps better than the second quarter and management’s outlook for no material sequential change.
ArcBest said it reduced its base liability insurance premiums while maintaining coverage limits during a recent renewal. However, it has retained higher risk on one of its excess insurance layers; that coverage has only been touched twice over the past 25 years.
The period also had the impact from an annual union wage increase.
Q4 asset-based outlook
Revenue per day was up 20% y/y in October as tonnage increased 15% and yield increased 4%. (Shipments were up 1% with revenue per shipment up 18%). October tonnage was down only 1% from September. It’s normally down 3.4%. Yield (ex-fuel) was again off by a low-single-digit percentage y/y, largely due to a 14% increase in weight per shipment.
It noted that weight per shipment growth will begin to moderate as the prior-year comparisons get tougher. It will continue to lean on its dynamic quote tool, which matches available network capacity to available transactional shipments in the market each day.
The unit’s OR normally deteriorates by 180 bps from the third to the fourth quarter, but management expects just 50 to 150 bps of erosion this year. The implied 91.4% OR guide (at the midpoint of the range) would be 480 bps better y/y. It said 2027 will likely be another positive step on its path to achieve 2028 financial targets .
Asset-light beats raised expectations
The company’s asset-light segment, which includes truck brokerage, beat raised expectations. Adjusted operating income of $14.4 million in the third quarter was ahead of the revised guidance ($10 million to $12 million) management provided in its August update . (The initial guide for the unit was $6 million to $8 million.)
Revenue of $446 million was 25% higher y/y as shipments increased 1% and revenue per shipment jumped 24% (including fuel). Purchased transportation expense (as a percentage of revenue) was up 10 bps y/y to 85%. Shipments per person per day increased 8% and selling, general and administrative expenses declined 2%.
The trends carried through October, with revenue per day 27% higher y/y (shipments up 8%, yield up 18%). Adjusted operating income is expected to range from $7 million to $10 million in the fourth quarter.
Why it matters? ArcBest is one of a few publicly traded LTL companies. Its quarterly results provide insight into a subsegment of trucking where few public datasets exist.

source_document.body:
Trimble reported higher third-quarter revenue and earnings Wednesday, but lowered its full-year recurring revenue growth forecast as weakness in European freight markets and slower demand for positioning services weighed on its outlook.
The Westminster, Colorado-based technology company (NASDAQ: TRMB ) reported third-quarter revenue of $967 million, up 7% year over year, while adjusted earnings per share reached 86 cents.
The results met Wall Street expectations, with the average estimate of four analysts surveyed by Zacks Investment Research was for revenue of $965.9 million and earnings of 86 cents per share, according to the Associated Press .
Annual recurring revenue (ARR) increased 10% to a record $2.564 billion, although growth fell modestly below management’s expectations.
Trimble maintained the midpoint of its full-year revenue forecast at $3.925 billion and slightly raised its adjusted earnings outlook. However, the company reduced its expected ARR growth to approximately 10%, down from its previous forecast of 12% to 14%.
CEO Rob Painter said Trimble’s performance reflected resilience despite a challenging supply chain environment and softer European demand, partially offset by strength in the U.S.
The company’s transportation and logistics business, which provides software for carriers, freight brokers and shippers , reported third-quarter revenue growth of 2% and ARR growth of 5%.
Operating margin in the segment increased 50 basis points to 26.3%.
European freight conditions pressure transportation growth
Painter said the European transportation market remained mixed, with freight volumes and spot pricing conditions weighing on the company’s recurring revenue performance.
Trimble’s Transporeon freight technology platform continued to demonstrate strong customer retention, with gross retention approaching 100% and ARR growth of approximately 9%.
However, lower freight volumes and a less favorable spot pricing mix compared with earlier in the year limited growth.
“In transportation and logistics, ARR growth was slightly below our first half, where the European freight market remains somewhat mixed,” Painter said during the earnings call.
The company also cited broader economic weakness in Europe, including inflationary pressures associated with the continuing conflict in the Middle East.
Painter said higher diesel prices presented both challenges and opportunities for the transportation business, as carriers and shippers increasingly seek technology to manage operating costs.
For the full year, Trimble expects transportation and logistics revenue and ARR to grow at mid-single-digit rates, while raising its operating margin expectation for the segment to 25%.
AI-powered freight procurement gains momentum
Despite slower overall transportation growth, Trimble reported increasing adoption of artificial intelligence across its freight technology platforms.
Painter said revenue from the company’s autonomous freight procurement and quotation solutions increased more than 20% year to date.
The technology automates processes including spot-market carrier selection, freight quoting and rate negotiation.
Strong bookings in the category are expected to support further revenue growth in 2027.
“If we look at transportation and autonomous procurement and autonomous quotation, those products have been in the market. We saw 20% growth year over year,” Painter said during the question-and-answer session.
He added that bookings were strong year to date, providing confidence in continued growth next year.
Trimble expands connected fleet and yard technology
Beyond AI-powered freight procurement, Trimble highlighted advances in routing, navigation and yard management technology.
The company’s PC*MILER web services platform processes more than 5.5 billion routing requests monthly.
Recent enhancements include advanced batch analytics and preferred-route settings that allow fleets to evaluate lane profitability and send optimized routes directly to drivers through the CoPilot navigation application.
Painter said the integration improves consistency between back-office planning and actual execution on the road, potentially increasing driver safety and operational efficiency.
Trimble also expanded its Dock and Yard platform, connecting appointment scheduling, carrier communications and yard management into a more integrated workflow.
The system provides facility operators with greater visibility into changing truck arrival times, helping them manage dock capacity and reduce delays.
Painter said reducing truck waiting times could allow customers to move the same freight volumes with fewer vehicles, improving asset utilization and helping address driver availability challenges.
Construction business drives overall growth
Trimble’s architecture, engineering, construction and operations (AECO) business remained the company’s largest growth engine.
The segment reported ARR growth of 13% to a record $1.636 billion, with revenue increasing 9% year over year.
Its operating margin expanded 170 basis points to 33.5%.
Field Systems reported 7% revenue growth and 5% ARR growth, supported by civil construction and geospatial demand.
However, weaker agricultural markets in South America, lower-than-expected positioning service subscription renewals and the planned exit from a low-margin third-party product line contributed to the company’s reduced ARR outlook.
Trimble also reported third-quarter adjusted EBITDA margin of 28.8% and free cash flow of $644 million through the first nine months of the year.
The company repurchased $224 million of its shares during the quarter.
For the fourth quarter, Trimble forecast revenue of approximately $1.046 billion and adjusted earnings of $1.16 per share at the midpoints of its guidance ranges.
Management expects full-year adjusted earnings per share of approximately $3.66, representing growth of about 17%.
Transportation business review remains unresolved
During the earnings call, analysts also questioned management about the ongoing strategic review of Trimble’s transportation business.
Painter reiterated that the company continues operating the business normally while evaluating its options.
“There’s no predetermined outcome or timeline as it relates to the review,” Painter said.
He emphasized that the transportation business continues to introduce products and deepen customer engagement despite uncertain freight market conditions.
The company also cautioned that its fiscal 2027 calendar will create an approximately $90 million headwind to reported revenue and operating income growth because of the timing of term-license renewals.
Trimble said the accounting-related calendar impact will not affect ARR or free cash flow.
Management expects to provide additional details on its 2027 outlook during the fourth-quarter earnings call in February.

source_document.body:
A Boeing 747-400 freighter jet operated by Central China Longhao Airlines arrived at East Midlands Airport on Monday, adding to the roster of cargo airlines now using the airport as a gateway to the United Kingdom market.
Central China Longhao Airlines will operate twice-weekly flights to East Midlands from Zhengzhou International Airport, the airport said in a news release.
China Central Longhao Airlines was restructured and established by Henan Civil Aviation Development & Investment Group in 2019 . As a state-owned airline and the main base airline in Henan Province, it played a key role in the construction of Zhengzhou international air cargo hub, and operates its fleet throughout Asia and into Europe.
China Central Longhao, which also calls itself Air Central, operates several smaller cargo jets within China, as well as two Boeing 747-400s. It says it plans to soon expand the fleet. International service currently connects Zhengzhou with Liege, Belgium; and Bengaluru, Chennai and Delhi, India. The U.S. Department of Transportation in March granted Air Central authority to operate flights to Chicago O’Hare and Los Angeles International Airport, but no operations to those destinations have started yet, according to flight tracking service Flightradar24.
East Midlands Airport, operated by the Manchester Airport Group, has a short-term goal of increasing cargo volume from a near-record 413,000 metric tons in 2025 to 500,000 metric tons by 2030, which would increase annual revenue by more than $11.2 million. Through September, cargo volume is up 5% year over year to nearly 211,000 metric tons. The airport recently advertised for a new head of cargo development.
Why It Matters: East Midlands has attracted more flight activity from China in recent years, coinciding with the surge in B2C e-commerce orders. The airport’s central location, lack of congestion, fewer night flying restrictions and cargo–focused infrastructure has attracted more freighter operators since the Covid crisis. East Midlands — home to the main U.K. air hubs of DHL Express, UPS and FedEx — is also benefitting from capacity constraints at other airports.
In April, YunExpress opened a cargo terminal at the airport to handle its own package freight arriving on Central Airlines flights from China. Last November, SF Express began operating from Ezhou to East Midlands carrying e-commerce goods on behalf of a distributor. One Air, a startup freighter operated based in the United Kingdom, in September 2025 began scheduled service between Hong Kong and East Midlands, with a focus on carrying e-commerce and electronics from China onboard its Boeing 747-400 cargo jets.

1958 Chevrolet Bel Air Gets First Cleaning in Decades, Morphs Into Stunning Survivor
14 photos
Photo: Theetravisb/YouTube
In 1958, General Motors celebrated 50 years in business with anniversary models for all divisions. For Chevrolet, this meant the introduction of new nameplates, including the iconic Impala , Biscayne, Yeoman, and Brookwood.
That same year also saw the discontinuation of the 150 and 210 models. However, Chevrolet kept both the Bel Air and Nomad in production. The latter retained its top position in the station wagon lineup, while the Bel Air slotted between the Biscayne and the Impala.
While the brand-new Impala was restricted to two-door body styles, the Bel Air was also available as a four-door sedan and hardtop. Much like its fancier sibling, the 1958 Bel Air is a one-year-old design. In 1959, Chevrolet gave its full-size car lineup a complete overhaul.
Several decades later, the Impala is arguably the most desirable Chevy of the 1958 bunch. The Bel Air doesn't get as much attention, and very few actually care about the four-door version. However, this sedan definitely deserves some time in the spotlight. It's one of those cool unrestored survivors.
Showcased by YouTube's "Theetravisb," this Bel Air spent most of its life with its original owner. The vehicle was retired in a backyard some decades ago and remained there even after the original owner passed away in 2012. More recently, however, it was auctioned off along with other things from the said estate, and found a new owner.
Fortunately, our host did not purchase the Chevrolet for parts or to flip after a bit of maintenance. He gave it a proper scrubbing, turning it into a stunning time capsule.
What sets this Bel Air apart from all the other undesirable Chevys? Well, for starters, it took decades of storage like a champ. This sedan is essentially rust-free, which is downright surprising given that it sat under full exposure to the elements for a while. Moreover, it's amazingly original .
It still rocks the original paint, which still looks good after proper cleaning and buffing. By the way, this Colonial Cream and Arctic White color combo isn't very common either. The interior looks even better, with the turquoise/teal upholstery showing next to no wear and tear (for a vehicle that's a whopping 68 years old).
The original engine is still under the hood, albeit it's not the desirable 348-cubic-inch (5.7-liter) W-series big-block V8. But it's not the entry-level 235-cubic-inch (3.9-liter) Blue Flame inline-six either. This Bel Air was fitted with the optional 283-cubic-inch (4.6-liter) small-block V8. It mates with an automatic transmission.
Although it may not be the most desirable Bel Air out there, this Chevy is a spectacular find. You just don't see unrestored survivors like this very often. Like our host puts it, this car should be in a museum. But I also think it deserves some time on the road. Check it out in the video below.

source_document.body:
A South Korean consumer group is asking regulators to stop Tesla from marketing “Full Self-Driving” to customers whose cars can’t legally run it. By Tesla’s own numbers, that covers 99% of the Teslas it sold in Korea last year.
Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty plans to file the complaint with the Korea Fair Trade Commission (KFTC) on Thursday, according to Reuters, which reviewed it. It comes just a week after a Seoul court threw out a refund lawsuit from Korean owners who paid for FSD.
Most Teslas in Korea can’t run FSD
It all comes down to where the car was built. The Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck come from US factories and enter Korea under the KORUS free trade agreement, which recognizes US safety standards. Those are the only Teslas that got “FSD (Supervised)” when Tesla switched it on in Korea late last year.
The problem is that those don’t represent the vast majority of Tesla vehicles sold in Korea.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The Model 3 and Model Y sold in Korea come from Giga Shanghai. There’s no equivalent deal with China, so those cars need Korean approval that FSD doesn’t have.
And that’s most of the fleet. Tesla Korea country manager Seo Young-deuk told lawmakers last month that FSD works on about 20% of Teslas registered in the country. Tesla has sold more than 170,000 Shanghai-built vehicles in Korea since 2023, per data it handed to the National Assembly, and sales of those China-made cars grew more than fivefold between 2023 and 2025.
Seo’s figure also clears up the conflicting eligibility numbers we flagged when Korean police booked 80 Tesla drivers for using illegal FSD unlock devices last month. A lawmaker’s data from May put it at 2.4%, while a data firm counted 20.7% in August. Tesla’s own testimony matches the higher one.
What the complaint alleges
For years, Tesla charged Korean buyers a one-time 9.043 million won (about $6,726) for FSD. It moved to a 150,000 won ($112) monthly subscription in August.
The complaint points to Tesla’s “coming soon” promotion last year and a demo video shot on Korean roads. Neither made it clear that FSD would only work on a small slice of the cars Tesla was selling. The group says Tesla knew that and kept pitching the package to every buyer anyway.
“Tesla generated substantial revenue by selling an expensive driver-assistance system to mass-market buyers who cannot use it for even a single day,” said Choi Young-suk, who heads automotive issues at the group.
It wants the KFTC to temporarily order Tesla to stop marketing FSD for ineligible cars. It’s also asking for fines and for the case to be sent to state investigators.
The KFTC is already looking at this. An official told Reuters the agency opened a probe into Tesla’s FSD advertising earlier this year and has received written responses from the company. Tesla didn’t respond to Reuters’ requests for comment.
Tesla only applied for approval last month
Tesla has collected FSD money from buyers of China-made cars in Korea for more than three years. But at an October 8 parliamentary hearing, Seo testified that Tesla had never formally asked the transport ministry to test FSD. Tesla filed for certification about two weeks later.

A computer rendering of India's Next Generation Corvette from an Indian Navy promotional video (Photo: Indian Navy)
SINGAPORE — India has signed a contract with two local shipbuilders to build eight Next Generation Corvettes (NGCs) for its navy, the country’s defense ministry announced Monday.
The Indian government awarded Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers Limited (GRSE) and Goa Shipyard Limited (GSL) a contract valued at 53,866.50 crore Indian rupees (approximately US $5.7 billion) to build five and three corvettes, respectively. A crore is a unit in the Indian numbering system equal to 10 million.
The corvettes will feature advanced missiles, weapons and sensor systems, allowing the ships to engage threats in the air, on the surface and underwater, according to the ministry. “The induction of these ships will significantly enhance the Indian Navy’s operational capabilities in safeguarding maritime trade routes, conducting anti-surface and anti-submarine warfare operations, strengthening coastal defence, undertaking littoral c ombat operations, and carrying out maritime presence and surveillance missions,” the ministry said in its announcement.
The ministry described the contract award as a “significant milestone,” noting that it marks the first project in which the Indian navy will design the ships and government-owned shipyards — known as Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) — will build them after being selected through a competitive process.
Both GRSE and GSL are majority owned by the Indian government.
GRSE said in its own announcement that the corvettes “will measure 127 metres in length and 17.6 metres in beam, with a specified deadweight tonnage of 4,950 tonnes” an d will be operated by a crew of 150, including 11 offic ers and 139 sailors.
The company added that the ships will be powered by a combined diesel and gas turbine–cross connect (CODAG-CC) propulsion arrangement driving two controllable-pitch propellers (CPP), giving them a top speed of 26 knots. The ships will be able to remain at sea for up to 14 days without replenishments.
The shipbuilder also provided further details on the corvettes’ planned equipment, stating that they will be armed with indigenous Medium Range Anti-Ship Missiles (MRAShM — although this weapon has also been called the Naval Anti-Ship Missile or NASM-MR), MRSAM medium-range surface-to-air missiles and 324mm torpedo tubes.
Other onboard weapons include the Leonardo 76mm Super Rapid naval gun, Russian AK-360 close-in weapon systems and 12.7mm remote weapon stations.
The corvettes will also feature electro-optical infrared search-and-track systems and multifunction surveillance, tracking and guidance radars — although neither the ministry nor the shipbuilders have identified the specific systems selected.

Xiaomi has released footage of its humanoid robots working a full 8-hour shift at its EV factory, sorting center console side covers for its cars. The company says the robots did it on their own, catching and fixing their own mistakes along the way.
If that’s fully autonomous, it’s truly impressive. But we’ve been disappointed by humanoid robot demos before, and Xiaomi left out the numbers that would let anyone check.
An 8-hour shift on the line
Xiaomi Tech posted the video on X on November 3, as the company picked up awards at the World Internet Conference in Wuzhen. It shows the robots pulling side covers from bins, carrying them to storage racks, and placing them into slots, with a running clock of cumulative working time and an “Autonomous, 100x Speed” label in the corner.
8 hours on the production line. 🤖 Xiaomi’s full-size humanoid robot takes on an 8-hour task at the Center Console Side-Cover Sorting Workstation at Xiaomi Auto Factory. Beyond sustained operation, it can autonomously detect and correct anomalies while coordinating with the… pic.twitter.com/brpO3S5bCn — Xiaomi Tech (@XiaomiTech_) November 3, 2026
According to Xiaomi, the robot covered the full day of production needs at that workstation. The company says it detected and corrected anomalies on its own and coordinated with the production line’s control system, calling it “another step toward real-world industrial deployment.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
This is the third milestone in a program Xiaomi has been running in public all year. In March, it put a humanoid in its Beijing EV factory as an “intern” installing self-tapping nuts. Xiaomi reported a 90.2% success rate over three hours, fast enough to meet the station’s 76-second cycle time. By July, it said that success rate was up to 98%, and it added two harder stations, including the side-cover sorting job from this week’s video.
Last December, Xiaomi’s CEO, Lei Jun, said the company plans to deploy humanoid robots in large numbers across its factories within five years.
Xiaomi also announced that its open-source Xiaomi-Robotics-1 AI model, pre-trained on 100,000 hours of real-world robot data, has started trial runs in Xiaomi staff apartments. In a 30-minute run, it completed more than 50 task chains across three rooms.
How autonomous was it
Xiaomi didn’t say how many parts the robots sorted, what the success rate was over eight hours, or how many times a human had to step in. It also didn’t explain how the robots stayed powered for a full shift: swapped batteries, a tether, or charging breaks.
And that matters, because “autonomous” in a robot video can mean anything. Tesla’s Optimus robots at the 2024 “We, Robot” event were remotely operated by humans , which Tesla didn’t disclose at the time. Last December, an Optimus took a suspicious tumble in a Miami demo , raising its hands to its head like a teleoperator pulling off a VR headset as it fell.
To be fair to Xiaomi, it has published success rates and cycle times for its earlier factory tests. That’s more than Tesla has ever shared about Optimus doing useful work, and Tesla now says it won’t deliver Optimus to outside customers until late 2027 .
Look at the wheels
The most interesting moment in the video comes around the 1:37 mark. In a segment Xiaomi labels “Dropped Material: Multi-Robot Collaboration,” a humanoid upper body mounted on a wheeled base rolls in to help the two legged robots.
A wheeled humanoid joins two legged robots in Xiaomi’s factory video (Image: Xiaomi)
It’s not the only thing on wheels in that scene, either. The bins of parts are shuttled around by autonomous mobile robots, the same kind of wheeled platforms that have been moving materials in car factories for years.
Electrek’s Take
If this demo was truly fully autonomous for eight hours, with the robots handling their own errors, that’s one of the more impressive humanoid demos we’ve seen. Xiaomi deserves credit for putting its robots on a real production line and publishing some real numbers along the way. But we’ve been burned by “autonomous” robot demos before, so we’ll wait for more details before getting too excited.
The wheeled robot is our favorite part of the video, though. It’s a great example of why you shouldn’t bet everything on the humanoid form factor. Wheels are far more efficient than legs on most terrain, and a flat factory floor is the best-case scenario for wheels. A wheeled base doesn’t burn energy just to stay upright, it’s more stable when carrying parts, it has room for a much bigger battery (which would solve that 8-hour power question), and it needs fewer expensive actuators.
The value in these robots is in the hands, arms, and the AI driving them. Legs make sense in homes with stairs, and maybe that’s where Xiaomi wants to take them eventually. But factories were designed around carts and forklifts, not people walking around carrying parts.

After a historic election defeat in one of the most expensive elections in US election history, the state of Texas has turned blue. Along with this come potential implications for Elon Musk and his companies.
The US midterm election was yesterday, and ended up in a stunning result, with Democrats taking control of both houses of Congress by wide margins, and flipping seats that had been considered safe around the nation.
Perhaps most notably, many of these seats were in Texas – a republican stronghold which saw a clean sweep, with the Democrats winning every statewide contest. Republicans maintained some state legislative power and won the State Senate, but as of this writing Democrats are currently ahead in the count for the State House.
Despite huge spending, Democrats won almost everything
The highest profile contest was for Texas Senate, where James Talarico won by a 55-43 margin. This race set the record for the most expensive Senate race in the nation’s history, with over half a billion dollars spent on this one seat alone.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
About half of the total money spent on the race came courtesy of republican PACs, a method by which companies and the ultra-wealthy can launder money into bribes to buy elections. And most of the PAC money in the race came from one man, Elon Musk, who spent $212 million to support the enormously unpopular and scandal-ridden outgoing Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton
That’s nearly half of the $474 million dollars that Musk put into this election cycle, suggesting that he saw this race of particular importance. And yet, his candidate lost miserably.
But the rout did not stop with Paxton. Paxton’s old job as AG is now going to be filled by Democrat Nathan Johnson. And Greg Abbott, the outgoing Governor, was defeated by Gina Hinojosa. Even the less high-profile races for court seats were swept by Democrats – three seats on the 15th Court of Appeals and four seats on the Texas Supreme Court.
And those results, even beyond the big-spending Senate race, could all matter quite a lot to Elon Musk.
Republicans rolled out the red carpet for Musk in Texas
In 2021, Musk announced that Tesla would move its headquarters to Texas , after Musk got in a spat with California government because he didn’t want to follow COVID restrictions for worker safety.
But the move wasn’t only about COVID restrictions – it was also about Musk’s vision of having more control over the business environment. And, by making allies with Ken Paxton and Greg Abbott, he has had quite a bit of control in Texas.
The two have rolled out the red carpet for Musk, giving him carte blanche in his adopted state.
Autonomous vehicle regulations have been changed, allowing driverless Robotaxis to operate where other states with more advanced regulations and transparency requirements would not. And many other laws benefitting Tesla and SpaceX have been passed. Paxton even sued Sam Altman , Musk’s chief AI rival, just weeks ago.
Perhaps more notably for Musk personally, Texas has promised to allow Musk to get away with more financial shenanigans than states with more established business regulations might.
With Tesla both headquartered and incorporated in Texas, it can now use special “ business courts ” instituted by Abbott at Musk’s own urging. If cases from these courts are appealed, they go to the 15th Court of Appeals, a court created by Abbott and filled with 3 hand-picked judges, intended to reduce the chance that a Democratic district court (say, one in Austin, whereTesla is headquartered) gets final say on any issue.
Several specific seats overseeing Musk went blue
But, the 15th Court of Appeals just had elections last night – and its three seats were flipped to Democratic control.
The 15th Court of Appeals also, just last week , stopped an inquiry into thousands of pages of emails between Abbott and Musk. The emails had been released , but are heavily redacted, with Abbott referring to the redacted portions as having “ intimate ” information in them.
And who made that request for inquiry into the emails? Gina Hinojosa, a name you might recognize, as she is the next Governor of Texas, as of last night.
As of yet, those emails have not all been released, so we don’t actually know exactly how much influence Musk was able to exercise over the state’s outgoing Governor. But given the changes we know about, the money Musk spent in Texas, and the thousands of pages of emails that have been redacted, it seems likely that there is something more to be found in them.
What does this mean for Musk’s companies?
So what does this all mean for Tesla, our main area of coverage here at Electrek ?
On a Texas state level, probably not all that much. There’s no reason that Democrats in the state would interfere with Tesla’s production of electric vehicles – in fact, they’d probably encourage it more than republicans do. Talarico has stated that he supports Tesla – it is a large employer in the state, after all.
And certainly, the national wins by Democrats could be a boon for EVs, given how hostile republicans have been to them (and Musk has been the single largest supporter of that hostility towards EVs).
The same likely goes for SpaceX – perhaps a blue Texas will be more restrictive of the company’s improper usage of protected habitats , or building of data centers , or whatever the hell is going on on twitter . But the core businesses of space launches and Starlink don’t seem likely to go anywhere.
What does it mean for Musk himself?
For Elon Musk, though, things could be different. Given his “intimate” relationship with Abbott, the extreme amounts of money he spent on Paxton, and the highly personal nature of his truly ridiculous attacks against Talarico, it seems unlikely that he will have a similar level of allyship with Texas government actors as he did in prior years. Talarico’s main anti-corruption message was seemingly aimed straight at Musk’s attempts to buy elections, after all.
And given his high levels of spending on a party that is outright hostile electric vehicles, it seems clear that his personal fortunes are far more important to him than the well-being of his companies.

Musk wants the deal so he can exercise more control over, and extract more personal wealth from, the combined entity.
But that scheme could rely on a favorable legal environment in Texas courts, an environment that just got less favorable.
And, given Musk’s penchant for childish lashings-out anytime he deems people insufficiently obsequious to his imagined greatness, could we see another situation where Musk encounters the tiniest amount of pushback from state government and then picks up his toys and leaves, as he already did in both California and Delaware? VW Explores Turkish Vehicle Production of Chinese-Developed Models
8 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
Volkswagen has a few problems in China. The biggest one is finding more customers for the vehicles it produces in China with its joint venture partners. Turkey could help with that, and the German automaker seems interested in local assembly of Chinese-developed models with Dogus Otomotiv.
This arrangement would offer the Wolfsburg-based group another way to use production capacity that its Chinese business no longer needs as badly due to shrinking demand in the People's Republic of China. During the first nine months of 2026, the group delivered 1.38 million vehicles in the PRC, down a whopping 30 percent from the same period last year.
Internal combustion models took a particularly dramatic hit as domestic manufacturers and their electrified models continued to gain serious ground. Keeping factories busy is considerably hard when the market that once absorbed millions of VWs starts buying fewer of them. Worse still, Volkswagen has spent decades building its Chinese operations around local demand.
The proposed Turkish partnership could provide an outlet. However, as of this writing, the agreement itself remains preliminary. Dogus Otomotiv confirmed that it had signed a letter of intent with the group to explore possibilities for producing said vehicles in the Republic of Turkiye. The disclosure is devoid of any confirmed models, production targets, or investment figures.
Hearsay suggests Volkswagen and Dogus could assemble FAW-Volkswagen models, and the rumor mill further suggests that CKD production is under discussion. CKD means completely knocked-down kit, and in this context, it stands for shipping disassembled vehicles from China to Turkey.
Photo: Volkswagen Rather than manufacturing every component locally, Volkswagen would use Chinese plants for component production and Turkey for vehicle assembly from these kits. The arrangement would provide additional work for its ailing Chinese plants while giving Dogus a more important role in the Turkish automotive industry.
Why Turkey, though? Per Automotive News, Turkey is a large new passenger vehicle market. Even more importantly, electric vehicles account for just under 20 percent of total registrations. That makes Turkey a useful market for a company that is trying to find customers for Chinese-developed gasoline models.
The potential connection to FAW-Volkswagen also needs highlighting because this joint venture has already started testing the export route. Its gasoline-powered models have reached markets in Central Asia and the Middle East, and the joint venture is also exporting vehicles to Madagascar. As such, the proposed Turkish operation would complement those efforts.
Volkswagen , meanwhile, is certainly thinking beyond Turkey. The group has increasingly moved away from its former Chinese approach. The group currently wants to use Chinese development and manufacturing capabilities for models that can find buyers elsewhere, as proven by the FAW-Volkswagen models exported to Madagascar, the Middle East, and Central Asia.
Oh, and by the way, Turkey isn't new territory for Volkswagen's manufacturing ambitions. The company abandoned plans for a factory there in 2020, citing the pandemic and economic uncertainties. That proposal, however, would have involved a dedicated production investment. Dogus, by comparison, would allow the German automaker to establish a production arrangement without committing to building an entirely new facility.

With the first Phase 3 data expected for Amgen’s MariTide next year, analysts are looking for evidence that the GLP-1 candidate is tolerable. Meanwhile, the company has begun testing an autoinjector formulation.
Amgen is racing toward readouts for its GLP-1 program, reaffirming plans for the candidate in its third quarter earnings report and beginning a study to support launching the product as an autoinjector.
The injectable drug candidate, MariTide, is differentiated on paper from incumbent GLP-1 products sold by Eli Lilly and Novo, notably by a half-life that Amgen believes can support dosing as infrequently as four times per year. In practice, however, “MariTide differentiation [is] still more of a show-me story,” BMO Capital Markets analysts said in a Nov. 3 note to investors.
“Management emphasized monthly dosing, potentially extending to four or six annual doses, and described gastrointestinal symptoms as generally short-lived despite prolonged pharmacologic activity,” BMO analysts said. “These observations are encouraging, but do not substitute for Phase 3 tolerability data.”
Amgen is expected to publish the first Phase 3 MariTide data next year. Ahead of the readouts, tolerability and maintenance, not weight loss, are driving the debate, Truist Securities analysts said in a Nov. 3 note, writing that they see “dose-escalation tolerability, durability and maintenance as key to validating differentiation.”
With pivotal data approaching, Amgen recently began another Phase 3 trial to study the home-based self-administration of subcutaneous MariTide using an autoinjector. The study has a primary completion date in June 2027, per ClinicalTrials.gov , leading TD Cowen analysts to predict in a Nov. 3 note that the trial could enable Amgen to launch MariTide as an autoinjector.
Amgen has been “pretty consistent in sharing that MariTide is expected ultimately to be delivered in a patient-friendly single-chamber handheld autoinjector,” Jay Bradner, executive vice president of R&D at the company, said on the third quarter earnings call. Amgen has “significant experience” with the delivery devices and has “taken a fairly standard approach,” Bradner added.
CFO Thomas Dittrich reaffirmed that Amgen expects capital expenditures of about $2.6 billion this year to scale manufacturing capacity for commercial growth and to prepare for a potential MariTide launch. 2027 Suzuki SV-7S Unveiled at the EICMA Show in Italy: I’m Suddenly More Nostalgic Than Ever
26 photos
Photo: Suzuki
My social media feed has been bombarded with videos from cruise ships lately. I love the sea, but I’m not a fan of that concept in particular. Some people are delighted by it, just as others love going to theme parks. Racetracks, mountain roads and car museums and garages are my idea of entertainment.
But I’ll tell you what else feels like a huge theme theme park: trade shows. SEMA and EICMA are on at the same time, and it’s a good thing they’re almost 6,000 miles apart (close to 10,000 km). Otherwise, people who love both cars and bikes might have had a hard time choosing between them. It’s been a while since I’ve attended either one of the two, but I must say it’s something any petrolhead should experience at least once in life.
Over the past few days we’ve been showing you updates from Italy on what’s happening in the world of two wheels. It seems everyone is on a fast-track to build new models, feature new tech, and fight for their customer’s attention. Manufacturers are filling the gaps in between what used to be the “standard categories”, which is both helpful and somewhat confusing at the same time as there are so many more options to choose from.
I’m not here to discuss how the market is changing though, but to give you a glimpse of Suzuki ’s new SV-7S. It makes me feel even more nostalgic than ever before, as two years have gone by since I’ve let go of my 1999 SV650S. My buddy Omar has been kind enough to let me ride it a few times since, but that’s also a story for another time. Right off the bat, I have to say Suzuki’s choice of name for the new model feels confusing to me.
Why call I an SV-7S when the engine inside is a 645 cc liquid-cooled V-Twin (and when the S used to have a front fairing and the N was the naked version)? It’s safe to say that it’s a marketing trick, the likes of which we’ve seen many times before (just think of Audi’s 40 TDI setups). I don’t mind that the GSX-8S/R has a 776 cc engine, and I didn’t even care that the SV-7GX had the same “problem” as the SV-7S.
Photo: Suzuki Anyway, I’m being nitpicky here, when I should probably just be happy that Suzuki at least didn’t give up on the V-Twin setup. In this day and age, I’m sure some motorcycle enthusiasts might think having 72 hp (at 8,500 rpm) and 64 NM/ 47 lb-ft of torque (at 6,800 rpm) is underwhelming, when BMW’s new M 1000 RS boasts about giving you access to 218 hp and 113 Nm of torque.
But I can assure you that an SV is more than enough for riding on public roads. The SV-7S is slightly heavier than its predecessors, but that’s just the cost we have to pay for the upgrades it has gotten over the years. I noticed the six speed transmission now has bi-directional Quick Shift System for clutch-less upshifts and downshift just like I only recently experienced on the Aprilia RS 660 .
The bike comes with Suzuki ’s Intelligent Ride System (S.I.R.S.), that includes a Drive Mode Selector, Traction Control with three mode settings (and OFF), ride-by-wire electronic throttle control, ABS, Easy Start System and even Low RPM Assist function. All these make the first-gen model feel like a dinosaur and I’d definitely love to ride them all back-to-back like I did with the Porsche 911 Turbo generations a few years ago.
The cast-aluminum 10-spoke wheels are wrapped in Dunlop ROADSMART III sport-touring tires, similar to what I last fitted to my bike when I went for an upgrade. The Japanese manufacturer is seemingly aiming for more comfort with the new bike, as the tapered aluminum handlebar is now wider and closer to the rider than it was on the SV650. The SV-7S certainly looks like a member of the family, and it’s as if even the muffler is the same like on the 2016 model.
Photo: Suzuki I realize most riders these days are fine will be fine with the 4.2-inch full-color TFT LCD, but I so wish we’d go back to the old way of doing things (at least give us an analog tachometer!). I get that the SUZUKI RIDE CONNECT+ smartphone integration could be helpful if you want to use the navigation system and get other sort of alerts, too. But riding my bike was often my only way to run away from the digital world and just live a little.
Also, isn’t it better to avoid distractions while you’re riding? For those of you who are keen to add the new SV-7S to your garage, you’re looking at a choice between three colors: Pearl Suzuki Deep Blue No.4, Glass Sparkle Black, and a mix between the latter and Mat Sword Silver. No, Yellow is not on the menu sadly. There’s no exact information on the pricing, but I expect it to be slightly below $8,000 at launch next summer. I’ll see if I can find a way to test one and see what it’s like.

Ocean Network Express more than quadrupled its second-quarter net profit and raised its full-year earnings forecast to $2 billion, as stronger freight rates and higher cargo volumes outweighed rising operating costs.
The Singapore-based container shipping company co-owned by three Japanese carriers reported net profit of $1.318 billion for the July–September quarter, compared with $285 million a year earlier . Revenue rose about 41% to $6.27 billion from $4.45 billion. The period represents the second quarter of its fiscal year ending March 2027.
The carrier increased its annual net profit forecast from $900 million to $2 billion and lifted its revenue outlook from $19.4 billion to $21 billion. It was the company’s second profit-guidance upgrade this fiscal year, following an increase from $300 million to $900 million after its first-quarter results.
ONE carried 3.396 million twenty-foot equivalent units, or TEUs, during the quarter, up 6.3% year-on-year. Its average freight rate increased to $1,709 per TEU from $1,252, helping offset higher fuel, vessel and other operating expenses.
“The second quarter delivered a strong financial performance, contributing to a solid first half of FY2026,” Chief Executive Till Ole Barrelet said in the company’s earnings announcement. “These results reflect our teams’ success in growing cargo volumes and achieving higher utilization despite a challenging operating environment.”
First-half revenue reached $10.812 billion, while net profit totaled $1.35 billion, compared with $371 million a year earlier. The figures show that nearly all of the company’s first-half profit came in the second quarter.
Demand on trans-Pacific routes benefited from U.S. inventory replenishment and shipments of equipment for data centers and industrial applications. Latin American and intra-Asian services also recorded positive demand, while Asia–Europe routes faced greater pricing pressure as available capacity increased.
Despite the stronger earnings, ONE expects seasonal demand to moderate and spot freight rates to ease during the second half. It nevertheless anticipates rates remaining above the levels assumed in its previous forecast, with a modest increase ahead of Chinese New Year.
The outlook remains sensitive to shipping disruptions in the Middle East and changes in routing through the Suez Canal. The company’s revised forecast assumes current conditions in the Strait of Hormuz persist through the fiscal year-end and Suez transits recover gradually. A return of more services to the Suez route could increase available capacity and put further pressure on freight rates.
“Looking ahead, we will adapt our network in response to evolving conditions, with safety remaining our top priority,” Barrelet said.
Why it matters: Higher freight rates and cargo volumes drive a sharp earnings rebound for Ocean Network Express, the 10th-largest ocean carrier, a good sign for the broader liner industy.

Speaking on third quarter earnings calls this week, Novo and Pfizer’s CEOs see little change to their Most Favored Nation drug pricing deals, which were signed with the Trump administration last year.
Big Pharma leaders presenting earnings this week largely shrugged off the potential of renewed risk ahead for drug pricing, with President Donald Trump’s Most Favored Nation initiative already embedded into assumptions.
Even with Democrats regaining control of Congress during Tuesday’s mid-term elections, executives were steadfast. Novo’s Mike Maziar Doustdar, reporting from Copenhagen Wednesday morning , was the first to speak to U.S. policy points after the blue wave.
“There’s always been a strong bipartisan support from both sides of the aisle for what we do,” Doustdar said. “We improve health at scale—whether you’re Republican or Democrat, you welcome that for your constituents.” He pledged to work closely with either party on “making sure that we can be a meaningful partner” to the U.S.
Leerink Partners warned that the Democrats could renew a push to lower drug prices but would likely have bigger issues to tackle first as they take control in Washington.
“Democrats likely have ‘bigger fish to fry’ than drug pricing in the near-term, in our view. But we do expect investigations related to drug pricing,” the firm wrote.
These investigations could focus on the confidential negotiations the administration conducted around MFN offering pharmas a chance to avoid tariffs, Leerink suggested.
While 2027 may not bring much change, Leerink warned that Trump himself has also suggested that he may seek to renegotiate MFN in 2028. America will also return to the polls that year to select a new president.
“Since the Trump administration’s voluntary tariff-avoidance deals with drug companies expire in December 2028, we have been assuming that President Trump could demand “a better bargain” from drug companies going into the November 2028 elections,” Leerink wrote.
BMO Capital Markets warned that the markets could be volatile for the industry today. “While Novo’s commercial beat is strong, we could see BioPharma shares face headwinds at open on U.S. Democrat ‘blue wave’ in midterms,” the firm wrote early Wednesday morning.

Bourla’s election outcome prediction was proven right. In a rebuke to Trump, Democrats retook both houses of Congress, flipping multiple key seats.
Bourla does not expect any changes this year for the MFN agreements, which Pfizer and other pharmas secured in order to avoid tariffs in 2025. But he admitted the policy woes of last year still weighed on him.
“It’s a very big contrast vis-a-vis what I was telling you a year ago. In 2025, I was really scared about the implications that either tariffs or MFN could have,” Bourla said.
But the CEO is confident that in working through those issues with the administration, there will not be any major policy surprises.
“Through the successful navigation of those issues, we brought the stability that is now projected to last and has brought, I think, this confidence back to the investor to invest in the in the industry in our sector,” Bourla said.
The art of the deal

AbbVie is doling out $100 million in cash to gain exclusive licensing rights to Nxera Pharma’s EP4 receptor agonist program in inflammatory bowel disease.
Under the terms of the deal, Nxera could collect up to $1.37 billion more in milestone payments, plus tiered royalties, according to a Wednesday release .
In exchange, AbbVie will gain access to Nxera’s EP4 agonist program, including global rights to develop and commercialize an oral small molecule called NXE0033744 in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). IBD is a group of chronic inflammatory conditions impacting the gastrointestinal (GI) tract—primarily ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease.
Japan-based Nxera, which rebranded from Sosei Heptares in 2024, culled the IBD program as part of a restructuring in November 2025 that also claimed 15% of the company’s workforce in Japan and the U.K. in the name of clearing the company’s “path to profitability.”
Discovered using Nxera’s NxWave platform, NXE0033744 is designed to address unmet need for patients with IBD that have not experienced satisfactory disease control. The asset is intended to work locally in the GI tract, reducing systemic exposure. NXE0033744 has already been tested in a Phase 1 trial among a group of patients with ulcerative colitis and in a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) challenge cohort.

Sunrun has doubled participation in its Puerto Rico virtual power plant to more than 60,000 customers, and the grid is putting those home batteries to work: It tapped into them for 18 straight days in October.
A virtual power plant (VPP) connects batteries across thousands of properties and coordinates them to supply power together.
Sunrun says its VPP network in Puerto Rico now includes nearly 70,000 batteries, frequently delivering 45 megawatts (MW) for four hours at a time. It has dispatched them more than 60 times since April, including daily deployments beginning October 13 during unusually hot weather.
For Puerto Ricans, who pay some of the highest electricity prices in the US, getting reliable power for all that money remains a problem. Residential electricity averaged 26.36 cents per kilowatt-hour in August, compared with a US average of 18.16 cents, according to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA).
Advertisement - scroll for more content
That makes the batteries already installed at homes pretty useful. The grid can pay to tap their stored energy when supplies get tight, putting existing equipment to work without waiting for a new power plant to be built.
Sunrun’s batteries get a second job
Sunrun’s network grew from around 4,000 customers in 2024 to more than 30,000 in 2025. It says it’s the largest aggregator in Puerto Rico’s Customer Battery Energy Sharing (CBES) program.
LUMA, the island’s grid operator, calls on CBES when it expects electricity demand or reserve needs to exceed available generation. Companies such as Sunrun then manage the battery response automatically.
Homeowners get paid for sharing energy and choose how much to keep for backup. Sunrun says most share a small portion of their total battery capacity; the company earns recurring revenue for operating the network.
Across the wider CBES program, LUMA reported in July that more than 90,000 participating customers had helped provide an average of 75 MW during generation shortfalls.
A larger VPP is needed
Puerto Rico’s reliability problem goes well beyond hurricanes.
Customers averaged 36 hours without power in 2025, even excluding major events, according to the US EIA. That’s up 19% from 2024. Mainland US customers generally experience about two hours a year under the same measure. Major events added another 23 hours of outages on the island.
More batteries can help, but the size of the shortfall still matters. In an April regulatory filing , participating aggregators said the program couldn’t prevent every rolling blackout in 2025 because some supply gaps exceeded its roughly 50 MW of four-hour capacity. They’re looking to enroll more batteries so the program can cover larger shortfalls.

This 2003 Mercedes G-Class Is a Classic Off-Roader Advertised at No Reserve
12 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
Our news feed is filled with all kinds of Mercedes G-Wagons, though it is mostly the range-topping AMG G 63 that gets the spotlight. Its predecessor, however, the first generation, does not get that much attention anymore, but the example pictured below deserves its fifteen minutes of online fame.
It is a 2003 model year in the G 500 configuration, and this means that it features a V8 engine under the hood. The mill has a 5.0-liter displacement, and with 292 horsepower (296 ps/218 kW) at 5,500 and 336 pound-feet (456 Nm) of torque from 2,800 to 4,000 rpm produced when the vehicle rolled off the line, it definitely does not impress by today’s standards. But let’s not forget that this machine saw the light of day more than two decades ago, and it remains a veritable off-roader.
The model returns the equivalent of 14.1 mpg US (16.7 l/100 km), so it is definitely not on the frugal side of things. However, it was never meant to be, just like it was never intended to be a dragster in disguise. With roughly 10 seconds needed to hit the 62 mph (100 kph) mark, it won’t blow your socks off, but to be honest, it is more than enough for daily drives, not to mention the occasional venture off the beaten path. Keeping the right pedal pinned to the floor will eventually make it max out at 118 mph (190 kph).
Mercedes offered multiple powertrain options for the first-generation G-Class, including several V8 units that were also mounted on the G 63 AMG, among others, as well as a bi-turbo V12. On the final iteration G 65, this mill, which had a 6.0-liter displacement, was officially good for 621 horsepower (630 ps/463 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque, enabling 0-62 mph in less than six seconds.
Photo: Cars&Bids Mind you, that’s more power than you’d get in the modern-day Mercedes-AMG G 63 , which has 577 hp (585 ps/430 kW) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque, but this model is quicker in a straight line, taking 4.3 seconds to reach the 62 mph (100 kph) mark from a standstill. The top speed is 149 mph (240 kph) with the AMG Driver’s Pack, or 137 mph (220 kph) without it, and the old one could sprint at up to 143 mph (230 kph).
The 2003 Mercedes-Benz G 500 in question is equipped with locking differentials at the front, center, and rear. It also features rear parking sensors, a power sunroof, a heated steering wheel, power-adjustable seats at the front with heating, a dual-zone climate control, and a few other things.
It also has quite a few modifications , such as the side-exit exhaust system, the matte green wrap, and the 22-inch wheels. The headlights and fender lights came from the aftermarket world, and so have the seat covers, headliner, and head unit.
Other than a dent on the front of the hood, there is nothing wrong with it, and this proves what we already knew: that this thing was built like a tank. The vehicle in question has 146,700 miles (236,100 km) on the clock, and by the looks of it, it has a lot of life left in it. The paint finish is Brilliant Silver Metallic beneath the wrap, and the interior is gray/black, though it now has a black and red look, as you can see in the images shared in the gallery.
Photo: Cars&Bids This Mercedes-Benz G 500 has a clean California title, and is located in Danville, CA. It has been reportedly registered in California, Texas, and Arizona since new. The Carfax report indicates a higher mileage than it is currently displayed, though the seller blames it on a clerical error, stating that they have filed a dispute claim with Carfax.
The recent service history shows that the tires were balanced in January 2026, and that several components were replaced in December 2025. These include the fuel filter, radiator, serpentine belt, serpentine tensioner, thermostat, thermostat housing/gasket, water pump, crankshaft position sensor, alternator, battery, and drive belt tensioner pulley. The differential fluid was also flushed, and the engine oil and filter were changed then, too.
This ride has been with the seller since January 2026, who has added some 4,000 miles (~6,500 km) since, and they now want it gone for an undisclosed reason. Thus, if you want a cool classic G-Wagen that looks very good (this writer thinks) on the outside, though with an interior that will instantly tell people you are not exactly loaded, then you should try to make it yours.
To do that, you will have to win the ongoing online auction on Cars&Bids, which will end on November 10, 2026. This Mercedes G-Class is advertised at the excitement of no reserve. The highest bid at the time of writing was $12,000, and you can check out this vehicle in more detail here .

MUNICH — A “snowball of activities” covering European orders and regional partnership agreements for Shield AI’s X-BAT fighter jet drone are set to be announced “soon,” according to the company’s cofounder and chief strategy officer.
Speaking to Breaking Defense today on the sidelines of the International Fighter Conference, Ryan Tseng said that the prospective deals and new industry pacts will be publicized when “we’re ready to announce them.”
He declined to comment on any aircraft quantities involved in the procurements, saying just “watch this space.”
Europe “can and should be a critical component of the [X-BAT] supply chain for Europe,” he said, noting it would make the region stronger at a “warfighting” level. Additionally, a “European sovereign” supply chain, makes the US more capable, stressed Tseng.
Andrew Hawkes, X-BAT director for Europe at Shield AI, also told Breaking Defense that the company is involved in “several active” sales campaigns for the autonomous, vertical take off and landing (VTOL) aircraft across the continent, though declined to disclose any individual customers.
The planned export business builds off a number of other key, regional developments. In June, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk reportedly said that Shield AI is planning on local production of X-BAT in cooperation with Poland. More recently, the firm announced a “strategic agreement” with Greece’s GEK TERNA, a critical infrastructure investor, based around a potential collaboration on “parts production, aircraft integration and long-term sustainment for X-BAT in Greece .”
Tseng’s assessment on orders comes after the artificial intelligence startup announced on Tuesday that a first, full-scale X-BAT prototype has completed assembly in Frisco, Texas. Next steps will see the aircraft undergo testing at the company’s facility in Newton, Kan., according to a company statement. Shield AI and the US Navy are jointly investing $400 million in X-BAT. Elsewhere, Tseng said that a per-aircraft cost for the autonomous drone could be brought down to $25 million, but for a higher-end sensor configuration, customers could expect to pay an extra $10 million.
The baseline $25 million figure works out around a quarter “the cost of a Eurofighter or an F-35 in Europe,” he explained. “We think from a lifecycle perspective, it would beat it [in production fighter jets] by a factor of 10″ based on comparable maintenance costs. “You can use far less crew to operate the aircraft” resulting in “savings across the board.”

Vauxhall Passes 100,000 Electric Vehicle Sales, Two Models Account for Nearly Half
12 photos
Photo: Vauxhall
Still twinned with Opel, the Vauxhall brand is celebrating a very important milestone. In the span of a few short years, it managed to sell precisely 102,852 electric vehicles in the United Kingdom. Its battery-electric journey started in 2019 with the electric version of the Corsa, which originally had 136 ponies and 50 kilowatt-hours to its name.
The current model packs a bigger punch, one additional kilowatt-hour, and more driving range to boot, specifically 265 miles (426 kilometers) instead of 209 miles (336 kilometers) in the WLTP. According to Vauxhall, a customer who purchased an electric Grandland from Drive Vauxhall Nuneaton pushed cumulative BEV sales past six figures.
Although the Grandland is a great compact model, the smaller Mokka Electric and the Corsa Electric have done most of the heavy lifting so far. The Mokka Electric leads the lineup with more than 26,000 registrations since 2020, whereas the Corsa Electric totals 23,000 units. Cumulative sales reached 10,000 vehicles in 2021, then passed 50,000 in 2023.
Vauxhall spent years building a broad electric vehicle lineup, with the British marque completing its commitment to offer electric versions of every passenger car in the range by the end of 2024. The current selection includes the Astra twins, Frontera , Combo Life, and Vivaro Life.
Naturally, the commercial vehicle side of the business also deserves attention. Vauxhall started offering an electric version of every van in 2021, and better still, it was crowned Britain's most popular electric van brand for three consecutive years. The Combo Electric is produced locally, with Vauxhall identifying Ellesmere Port as the UK's first volume manufacturing plant dedicated exclusively to battery-electric vehicles.
Photo: Vauxhall Going back in time, the British company's electric ambitions are rooted in the range-extender technology introduced by the Ampera back in the 2010s. Mechanically related to the Opel Ampera, Chevrolet Volt, Holden Volt, and the Cadillac ELR, the OG hides an internal combustion engine underhood.
Said engine does not directly power the wheels under normal conditions. It usually turns on to spin a generator that recharges the traction battery. Three clutches lock or unlock the planet carrier, sun gear, and ring gear to shift between purely electric and range-extended operation. The internal combustion engine drives the front wheels only at higher vehicle speeds, when the battery is depleted.
Between the Vauxhall Ampera and the full-electric Corsa, the Ampera-e was supposed to serve as the brand's first mass-market electric vehicle. While its Opel-branded sibling enjoyed limited European commercial success, General Motors ultimately canceled the right-hand-drive Vauxhall model before its planned UK market release.
Turning our attention back to the present day, Vauxhall has also expanded its electric vehicle lineup with high-performance versions. The Mokka GSE and Corsa GSE come to mind, with prices currently starting at £36,170 and £34,495, respectively, OTR. By comparison, the most affordable full-electric Corsa on sale today in the United Kingdom is advertised from £26,780 by its maker.
"From the revolutionary Ampera to today’s fully electrified car and van range, we have remained a champion of EVs, and our focus is to continue making electric mobility more accessible and attainable for British drivers and businesses," said Eurig Druce, Vauxhall Managing Director and Stellantis UK Group Managing Director.

710-HP Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat Joins Texas Police
69 photos
Photo: Texas Department of Public Safety - North Texas Region on Facebook
Back in the '90s, the American police fleet was full of body-on-frame sedans with V8 muscle. Sport utility vehicles started gaining ground in the 2010s. The Explorer-derived Police Interceptor Utility is a fine pursuit-rated sport utility vehicle by modern standards, but alas, it simply doesn't hold a candle to a Hellcat-powered bruiser like the Durango SRT Hellcat.
Per a recent social media post, the Texas Department of Public Safety has a new addition to its North Texas fleet. Someone clearly decided that a Police Interceptor Utility wouldn't make quite the same impression, that's for sure! "All that horsepower. One mission: Public Safety," reads the department's Facebook post, and that's all the information the department offered.
Given the aforementioned, we don't know if said 710-horsepower sport utility vehicle would handle appearances at public events, highway enforcement, regular patrols, or emergency response. Finished in black, the ominous-looking Dodge wears a substantial bull bar up front and emergency lights on said bull bar.
As expected from a police vehicle, additional lighting sits near the top of the windshield. There is no roof-mounted light bar to speak of. Whether its omission has anything to do with aerodynamic drag at 180 miles per hour, which is this model's factory-rated top speed, we don't know for sure.
Department logos can be seen on the doors. The Texas DPS has not published any photos of the cabin, which makes it impossible for us to determine what kind of interior mods are featured. All in all, the visible mods do not reveal its assignment.
Photo: Texas Department of Public Safety - North Texas Region on Facebook I would resist calling this fellow a dedicated pursuit vehicle until an official explains its role. Police departments sometimes use high-performance vehicles for public engagement and community appearances, particularly when they want something that gets enthusiasts talking. Case in point: they even got us talking!
Anyhow, this particular example of the breed certainly qualifies. Beyond its 6.2-liter supercharged HEMI engine, which develops a massive 645 pound-feet (875 Newton-meters) of twist, the Durango SRT Hellcat occupies a unique space in the market. For starters, what other unibody sport utility vehicle with a supercharged V8 engine is produced nowadays?
Also worth noting, the Jailbreak customization platform unlocks a bunch of restrictions, offering more than six million potential customization combinations. Then there's the actual platform, which traces its roots back to the DaimlerChrysler era. As far as we know, the WD-series Durango is the oldest of its kind as of November 2026.
The WD came out in 2010 for the 2011 model year, and its platform wouldn't have been possible without Mercedes. Under the skin, the Durango is related to the W166 M-Class (a.k.a. GLE) and the larger X166 GL-Class (a.k.a. GLS). The current-gen GLE and GLS, by comparison, can't do better than twin-turbo V8s with a displacement of 4.0 liters.
From the standpoint of operating costs, the Durango SRT Hellcat is a very bad proposition. 13 miles per gallon combined means 18 liters per 100 clicks in metric speak, and that's a lot of gas money on a yearly basis. The more interesting question, however, isn't whether the department can afford the fuel. It's why the Texas DPS chose this particular model instead of the Police Interceptor Utility.

1961 DeSoto Hardtop Fetches $80K at Auction, Becomes the World's Most Expensive
14 photos
Photo: Richmond Auctions
Established in 1928, DeSoto slotted between Plymouth and Dodge in the Chrysler division hierarchy, competing with brands like Studebaker, Hudson , Willys, and Pontiac. In 1933, DeSoto was repositioned above Dodge. Phased out in 1961, DeSoto is now one of the many orphan Big Three divisions.
DeSoto was quite successful in the 1950s, moving over 100,000 units per year early in the decade. However, sales dropped to under 40,000 units in 1958, a recession year, and didn't recover in 1959. With Dodge moving upmarket and Chrysler offering a more affordable Newport model, DeSoto didn't survive past the 1961 model year.
The 1961 DeSoto was produced for only a few months, mainly from left-over stock. The company put together only 3,034 units, making the 1961 DeSoto the rarest iteration out there. The figure included 911 two-door hardtops and 2,123 four-door sedans.
In addition to being rare, the 1961 DeSoto also stands out by not having any nameplates. Both the Fireflite and Adventurer badges were dropped after the 1960 model year. Additionally, the 1961 DeSoto is a one-year-only automobile by design thanks to a two-tiered grille.
On the flip side, the final-year DeSoto is far from desirable today. While some older Adventurer models fetch six-figure sums at public auctions, the 1961 DeSotos barely exceeded the $30,000 mark. And that's precisely why a 1961 hardtop selling for $80,000 is a noteworthy event.
It happened at a Richmond Auctions event in late October, where this red example went under the hammer at no reserve. The gavel fell at exactly $80K, updating a $55,000 record that had been standing since 2009. Another hardtop that sold for $49,500 in 2013 rounds off the list of 1961 DeSotos that fetched over $30,000. Both were well-maintained, low-mileage examples.
The surprisingly high amount was paid for one of the only 911 two-door hardtops produced that year. But this DeSoto is also a fantastic automobile: factory correct, flawless inside and out, and still sporting its original drivetrain .
Like all DeSotos built for the 1961 model year, this hardtop packs Chrysler's B-series 361-cubic-inch (5.9-liter) V8 engine. The mill was rated at 265 horsepower and 380 pound-feet (502 Nm) of torque. The car was equipped with the standard three-speed TorqueFlite automatic with the push-button configuration.
The classic spent its recent years in the prestigious McCandless collection. The same event saw a 1955 Dodge La Femme cross the block for $120,000, a world record for the rare and short-lived nameplate.
Although this DeSoto is the most expensive 1961 model out there, it's far from being the priciest overall. In recent years, six Desotos from the late 1950s fetched over $200,000. The record is being held by a 1959 Adventurer convertible that changed hands for $330,000.

Sanofi has discontinued an early-stage STAT6 degrader program licensed from Nurix Therapeutics, a decision analysts say is related to the asset itself or Sanofi’s strategic reprioritization rather than the drug class more broadly.
Nurix Therapeutics shares fell more than 30% after market close on Tuesday after the biotech disclosed that Sanofi was discontinuing development of a STAT6 degrader licensed from Nurix—but analysts don’t see the move as a critique of the drug class or as extremely damaging for the company.
“While NRIX has limited visibility into the full data package, initial discussions have pointed to molecule-specific attributes of SAR448272 rather than a target-related issue,” Truist Securities wrote in a Tuesday evening note.
Leerink Partners analysts, who spoke with investor relations (IR) representatives at Sanofi, also relayed that the discontinuation was specific to that asset.
“We connected with IR, who stated that the decision was based on ‘emerging nonclinical findings that did not warrant continued development in atopic dermatitis,’” the firm said in a Tuesday evening note.
The program cut comes just two months after Nurix collected a $10 million milestone payment from Sanofi as the pharma kicked off a Phase 1 trial for SAR448272 in type 2 inflammatory diseases.
Sanofi and Nurix linked up in 2019 to leverage the latter’s DEL-AI drug discovery platform to identify novel agents that use E3 ligases to induce the degradation of specified proteins. In 2025, the French pharma picked up a license extension option for two programs targeting transcription factors for autoimmune and inflammatory diseases, according to Nurix’s Tuesday release . One target was undisclosed. The other was STAT6.
Now, Sanofi has informed Nurix of its decision to discontinue a Phase 1 first-in-human trial of the STAT6 degrader SAR448272, and to terminate the program, the San Francisco–based biotech said on Tuesday.
Shares of Nurix fell by as much as 38% in post-market trading Tuesday, recovering only slightly to $16.15 per share in pre-market trading on Wednesday.
Truist viewed Nurix’s post-market stock drop as “an overreaction,” writing that while the discontinuation was “disappointing given the potential upside and upcoming peer data catalyst, STAT6 was not included in our valuation, limiting the direct impact on our base case.”
