Once considered undruggable, STAT6 is emerging as a hot target in immunology, where Sanofi is a key player.
The STAT6 protein is crucial for IL-4–mediated biological responses. It is believed to play a role in several dermatologic and respiratory diseases, according to Recludix Pharma, with whom Sanofi is developing a STAT6 inhibitor in a Phase 1 trial .
With the fate of Nurix’s STAT6 program “unclear,” Oppenheimer said the biotech’s story now rests primarily on the fate of a separate collaboration with Roche. The Swiss pharma in June paid Nurix $700 million upfront —with milestones totaling a potential $2.3 billion—to co-develop and co-commercialize bexobrutideg, a Bruton’s tyrosine kinase (BTK) degrader, for B cell malignancies as well as immunological and neurological conditions.
The drug is currently in Phase 1/2 studies in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL).
Nurix “remains well-positioned in CLL” with bexobrutideg, Oppenheimer said.

source_document.body:
View along a row of static aircraft during the Royal International Air Tattoo at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, England, on July 19, 2025. (Photo by Jon Hobley | MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
WASHINGTON — The Royal International Air Tattoo, an annual airshow in the United Kingdom, will permanently move to a new location , organizers announced today.
The decision to shift from RAF Fairford, the air base that has hosted the event for four decades, comes after the 2026 edition of RIAT had to be cancelled due to the use of that airfield for US B-1 bombers operating against Iran. Those bombers were later relocated back to the US due to concerns over a terrorist attack by Iran on the base.
The new location for the show going forward will be MOD Boscombe Down, roughly 90 minutes south of Fairford by car and equidistant from London. The new location “provides an outstanding platform for RIAT’s future ambitions, offering the space, capability and flexibility required to support the event’s continued evolution,” organizers said in a statement.

For many years, RIAT was seen as more of a public airshow. However, over the last decade, the defense establishment has increasingly used the event to showcase capabilities and make announcements, sometimes to the detriment of the biennial Farnborough Airshow.

Man Buys New 2024 Corvette Z06 Convertible for $152,415, Drives 1,200 Miles, Sells for $115,000

Photo: Cars & Bids
Here's yet another C8 Z06 that got bought well. Basically, a $37,000 discount for a barely-driven Z06 Convertible, meaning the buyer avoided that steep initial depreciation while acquiring a supercar with a super spec. The seller? Owning this car cost them approximately $31 per mile, on top of their initial $152,415 investment.
Myself, I don't mind the $115,000 valuation, especially when you factor in the Z06 Ultimate Performance and Carbon Fiber Aero packages. Would I have preferred it if this was a 3LZ model? Yes, absolutely. But there's nothing wrong with a good 2LZ, especially if it comes with the optional front-axle lift system, which this does.
Also, this is a convertible, not a coupe. I know that doesn't matter to some people - I think you can be just as happy with the coupe, since the top comes down. But others will always prefer the ability to drop top electrically. It's faster, more efficient, and let's face it, more practical.
In terms of visuals, this Z06 is very pretty to say the least. I love the Ceramic Matrix Gray colorway, which tends to look white depending on lighting. It also allows for a high contrast look once paired with various dark trim pieces, like you get with the aforementioned Carbon Fiber Aero package.
Other highlights include the 20" front and 21" rear Spider Design forged wheels, leather upholstery, power-adjustable heated and ventilated GT bucket seats, the Z07 suspension, LED headlights, a head-up display, Brembo brakes, black exhaust tips, Torch Red seat belts, cruise control, heated steering wheel, wireless CarPlay and Android Auto, dual-zone automatic climate control, and quite a bit more.
You also get a wide range of electronic driver aids, such as rear park assist, rear cross traffic alert, side blind zone alert, the Intellibeam-Auto high beam system, a following distance indicator, forward collision alert, lane keep assist with lane departure warning, and automatic emergency braking.
Photo: Cars & Bids The options alone cost nearly $25,000. Among them the $9,000 Z06 Ultimate Performance package and the $8,500 Carbon Aero pack. 2LZ or no 2LZ, this is a lot of car for $115k. A lot of supercar, that is.
As for performance, it all comes down to the mid-mounted 5.5-liter LT6 V8 engine. It's putting down 670 horsepower and 460 lb-ft of torque, with everything getting sent to the rear wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
I'm going to be straight with you guys. I don't recall a whole lot of nicer Z06 Convertibles for this type of money. I'm not saying this is any kind of a world record, but it's pretty solid value. One car I recall is this 2024 Z06 Coupe with 1,500 miles on the clock that sold for $110,500. Cheaper but, again, a Coupe, not a Convertible.

GM Prepares Hybrid Chevrolet Traverse, GMC Acadia, Buick Enclave
6 photos
Photo: Chevrolet
General Motors spent one too many years telling American drivers that battery-electric vehicles are the future. As many of us knew from the very beginning, putting all eggs in one basket is a very poor tactic. Better late than never, Detroit's largest automaker has realized that giving its customer pool multiple powertrain choices is better than imposing electric nonsense on everyone.
GM's mea culpa includes three hybrid sport utility vehicles, namely hybrid versions of the Chevrolet Traverse, GMC Acadia, and Buick Enclave. All three models would generate substantial business. According to Reuters, which cites people familiar with the automaker's domestic plans, all three will be produced at the Lansing Delta Township factory in Michigan.
Designed as the company's first green factory, LDT specializes in large crossovers. The complex operates as a complete production site, which means that LDT also handles metal stamping and body welding. The move to bring three hybrid crossovers to market will certainly make dealers happy, dealers who have been asking for hybrids for years now.
General Motors has confirmed an investment in the Lansing complex for hybrid production, but as opposed Reuters, the automaker hasn't yet identified the hybrid models planned for LDT. The launch schedule remains a mystery as well, and don't even dare ask about technical details.
There is, however, good reason to start with said three-row models. The Traverse, Acadia, and Enclave share much of their underpinnings. Chevrolet, as ever, handles the mainstream crowd, Buick is the premium alternative, and GMC mixes a premium character with rugged capability.
Photo: Chevrolet In combustion-only form, all three offer three-row seating. This makes fuel consumption a relevant concern. Families who spend plenty of time behind the wheel definitely prioritize efficiency, and hybridization is the right approach in this segment as of this writing.
Hybrid powertrains make large SUVs more appealing without asking customers to change how they use them. An internal combustion engine is still featured, there is no need to plug them in, and servicing costs aren't particularly different from purely internal combustion models.
GM is understood to be developing both self-charging and plug-in hybrids. Chief executive officer Mary Barra has already underlined that GM needs a broader electrified offering, and the key word here is "broader." The person in charge of General Motors also said that hybrids would cover multiple segments.
More curiously, Barra made it clear that hybrids wouldn't require additional engineering and capital expenditure beyond the company's existing plans. That seems a bit odd when you remember that Cadillac once intended to become fully and exclusively electric by 2030, but hey, who am I to question the CEO?
To support hybrid production at LDT, the automaker intends to redirect $500 million in federal funding originally awarded to support electric vehicle manufacturing in the state of Michigan. As if that wasn't enough, approximately $1.25 billion will be invested by General Motors in the Lansing site to accommodate hybrid vehicle production.

President Donald Trump delivers remarks the day before the midterm elections, Nov. 2, 2026, at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. Credit: Official White House Photo by Joyce Boghosian
Posted By: Colin McClelland November 4, 2026
Democrats’ capture of Congress raises the prospect of greater scrutiny of President Donald Trump’s mining and energy agenda, even as pressure to lower electricity costs could create an opening for a bipartisan permitting deal.
The party won control of the House of Representatives and Senate in Tuesday’s midterm elections, setting up divided government from January. Investors face the possibility of tighter regulation of data centre construction and closer examination of federal investments, while permitting reform could provide common ground on energy affordability, according to assessments from BMO and Wood Mackenzie.
“While we see the likelihood for permitting reform, how policy is legislated and implemented remains a risk to the U.S. economy,” David Brown, Wood Mackenzie’s director of global integrated energy research, said Wednesday. “Entrenched partisanship could fuel policy stagnation and regulatory confusion.”
For miners, the election puts the durability of Trump’s mining agenda to the test. Democrats have already challenged Washington’s financial stakes in mining companies and questioned the terms of a bipartisan permitting proposal. Their stronger negotiating position could reshape that legislation, while scrutiny of data centres could affect a source of growing copper demand.
Greater scrutiny
Democrats’ concerns about federal mining investments predate the election. Senator Martin Heinrich and Representative Jared Huffman, the senior Democrats on the Senate energy and House natural resources committees, sought a watchdog investigation in August into financial safeguards and potential conflicts when Washington acts as both investor and regulator.
They asked the Government Accountability Office to examine how agencies assess investment risks, protect taxpayer funds and manage permitting decisions involving companies in which the government holds stakes.
Democratic control could also bring investigations into presidential family interests in companies, while appointments of officials, ambassadors and judges could be blocked or delayed, BMO said in a Wednesday note.
The prospect of stronger regulation could slow data centre development and soften inflationary pressures, the bank said. That contrasts with Wood Mackenzie’s assessment that pressure to lower electricity costs could encourage both parties to accelerate infrastructure approvals.
Gold gains
Gold and copper face different pressures from the result, according to TD Securities strategists Ryan McKay and Bart Melek.
Constraints on Trump’s fiscal agenda could limit further spending, helping push the dollar and longer-term Treasury yields lower and lifting gold back above $4,000 per oz., they said in a Wednesday note.
Copper initially weakened on the prospect of increased scrutiny of artificial intelligence data centre construction before recovering as tight physical supplies, particularly in China, supported prices, they said.
Potential AI regulation could challenge a major source of stock market gains, according to Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell (LSE: AJB). The British investment platform had £126 billion in administered assets at Sept. 30.
“Given that AI has been the key to considerable stock market wealth creation in recent years, the prospect of red tape could put the brakes on this hot investment theme,” Mould said in emailed comments. “However, a positive market reaction implies that certain investors are welcoming the potential that Trump’s political power may be curbed somewhat.”
Gold rose 2.7% to $4,038 per oz. in the early trading snapshot cited by Mould, who suggested investors were adding protection against uncertainty over Trump’s response to the result.
The election leaves metals tariffs largely outside Democrats’ immediate reach. Section 232 duties on steel, aluminum and copper products remain under presidential authority, as would potential tariffs on refined copper from January, BMO said.
Those tariffs survived Democratic gains in the 2018 midterms and are widely viewed as having strong bipartisan support, the bank added.
Permitting bargain
Wood Mackenzie’s case for a permitting deal rests on a shared incentive to reduce energy costs and a proposal already backed by senators from both parties.
The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, introduced before the election, would overhaul federal environmental reviews and permitting. Republican senators Shelley Moore Capito and Mike Lee joined Democrats Sheldon Whitehouse and Heinrich in sponsoring the proposed legislation to accelerate energy and mineral development.
The package would strengthen review deadlines, restrict agencies’ ability to revoke permits and narrow the window for legal challenges. Wood Mackenzie highlighted two-year environmental impact reviews, a 150-day litigation window following environmental approvals and a nine-month timetable for evaluating dredge-and-fill permits needed for new gas pipelines.
But Democratic support for reform does not guarantee support for the existing compromise.
Huffman questioned the Senate package in a September statement , seeking stronger protections for communities, wildlife and renewable energy projects. He argued that Democrats should wait for greater negotiating power after the election.
“Folding our hand now or in the lame duck makes no sense,” Huffman said.
Trump would retain veto authority, and the impact of any legislation would depend on implementation by executive agencies, Wood Mackenzie cautioned. New renewable energy subsidies proposed by Democrats would be unlikely to overcome a presidential veto, the consultancy said.
Power pressure
Rising electricity costs could provide an incentive for compromise. Wholesale U.S. power prices could climb 46% between 2026 and 2035 under Wood Mackenzie’s base case as data centres and other infrastructure expand, the consultancy said.
It forecasts 166 gigawatts of net new gas-fired generating capacity over that period. Much of that development would require additional pipelines, making gas infrastructure approvals a potential constraint on electricity supply.
“Without reform, midstream bottlenecks are likely to return, stifling upstream investment and pushing regional gas and power prices higher, most acutely in the power-hungry Northeast,” Siddhant Warrier, Wood Mackenzie’s North American power research analyst, said. “Prolonged pipeline delays would also slow data center development, a high priority for both parties.”
Transmission construction faces similar pressure. High-voltage line completions in the 2020s have been running at less than half the rate of the previous decade, according to the consultancy.
Faster approvals would address only part of that problem. Allocating the cost of lines that cross utility territories and benefit several states remains contentious. State governments would become more important if federal negotiations stall because they oversee retail electricity, utility regulation and much project siting, Wood Mackenzie said.
The first test comes before the new Congress takes office. The Senate has scheduled a procedural vote for Nov. 9 on advancing the legislation serving as the vehicle for permitting reform, opening negotiations over whether a deal can pass in the remaining weeks of Republican control.

Pierroberto Folgiero, Fincantieri's CEO, tours its Wisconsin shipyard. (Photo courtesy of Fincantieri Marinette Marine.)
PARIS — Italian defense companies Leonardo and Fincantieri this week announced a restructuring of their Orrizonte Sistemi Navali (OSN) joint venture, which the CEOs of both firms say could trim the time required to build a frigate by 18 months.
The joint venture, which has existed for over two decades, will return to its former model, in which OSN serves as an overarching integrator of an entire warship. The move would effectively change the conglomerate’s current approach, where Fincantieri and Leonardo generally manage separate aspects of the same ship.
The heads of Leonardo and Fincantieri, Lorenzo Mariani and Pierroberto Folgiero, signed a Letter of Intent at the Euronaval defense show here on Tuesday. Executives said the renewed joint venture, in which Fincantieri owns 51 percent and Leonardo 49 percent, would be more competitive in European and export markets.
“Italy has a strong industrial setup in the naval domain, which enables us to perform effectively and deliver faster than in the past. One of OSN’s key objectives will be precisely to shorten these lead times,” Pierroberto Folgiero, the CEO of Fincantieri, told reporters on the sidelines of Euronaval.
Folgiero said executives set a goal of cutting the delivery window for FREMM frigates from 54 to 36 months, a key “test case” that could determine whether the companies’ combined shipbuilding prowess can deliver a vessel on a timeline similar to the Korean industry.
The joint venture’s roster spans several vessel types, including the Italian Navy’s light multirole offshore patrol ship class, the PPX, and the FREMM EVO, an evolution of the Italian Navy’s European Multi-Mission Frigate program.
In September, OSN additionally signed a contract valued at €3.7 billion ($4.2 billion) with OCCAR (Organisation Conjointe de Coopération en matière d’Armement) for the development, production and initial in-service support for two new-generation DDX destroyers to equip the Italian Navy.
In July, Portugal awarded Fincantieri an approximate €3.9 billion ($4.4 billion) order to build three FREMM EVO frigates, with deliveries planned for 2029-2030. In September, Italy and Greece also finalized an agreement to transfer two Carlo Bergamini-class FREMM frigates from the Italian Navy to Athens, where Fincantieri will oversee the technical transfer and modifications of these warships.

Lufthansa Cargo
By Stuart Todd
4 November 2026
Lufthansa Cargo increased its base yields by 14% year on year in the third quarter, with strong demand and constrained capacity supporting pricing power, even as Middle Eastern airlines restored services.
Overall yields rose 22%, as the carrier also successfully passed-on higher fuel costs. Adjusted EBIT more than tripled, to €162m ($182), with margin reaching 15.6%, up from 6% a year ago.
Lufthansa Group CEO Carsten Spohr told analysts on a conference call in Frankfurt yesterday that the strong performance came during what is usually the seasonally weakest quarter for airfreight.
“The strong performance reflects a very robust demand environment. Capacity increased by 5%, driven by double-digit growth in belly capacity, mainly due to the now fully integrated belly capacity of [Italian airline] ITA. Chargeable weight increased by 7% and, as a result, load factors increased by more than three percentage points. At the same time, pricing remained very strong,” he said.
One forwarder told The Loadstar the drivers of cargo carriers’ pricing power, and the implications of returning Middle East capacity, differed between the major east–west trades, explaining: “Capacity is extremely tight on the Far East-North America tradelane – where obviously the return of Middle East capacity is not an issue – driven by phenomenal demand from the hyperscaler boom and which continues to pump up rates.”
Mr Spohr also highlighted the strength of Asian demand and Lufthansa Cargo’s growing exposure to transpacific flows.
He said: “Demand remains particularly strong in Asia-Pacific, with India standing out as a key growth market. Transpacific flows are becoming increasingly important for us, even though we’re on the other side of the world.
“Currently, demand is driven by express deliveries on the one hand and by high-margin verticals on the other. These include semiconductors and IT equipment, but also pharma and automotive.
“More broadly, Lufthansa Cargo continues to benefit from current supply chain disruptions around the world, but has also structurally improved its positioning by focusing on those markets and products that matter most in the air freight business and create the highest yields and value.”
In a more detailed review of Lufthansa Cargo’s Q3 performance, the group said strong market demand had continued “in the context of the significantly changed market environment due to the conflict in the Middle East and the corresponding reduction in competitors’ capacities in the region”.
Reduced market capacity and sharply higher fuel costs had led to a significant increase in yields compared with previous quarters.
Global revenue increased 26%, “with broad-based regional growth”, while ex-Asia yields were “robust, despite de minimis pressure”. Revenue from temperature-controlled freight rose 33% year on year.
Turning to the outlook, group CFO Till Streichert told analysts Lufthansa Cargo’s year-to-date earnings had reached €361m, with further upside expected for the full year.
“Adjusted EBIT of Lufthansa Cargo is likely to comfortably surpass €500m in full-year 2026, with possibly even more positive dynamics. While this upside potential is very likely to materialise, a high degree of uncertainty still remains, as visibility in the air freight business is usually limited to about two weeks booking in advance.”
On whether current pricing power would endure as Middle Eastern capacity returned, the forwarder pointed to signs of easing pressure on Asia-Europe.
“Emirates, Etihad, and Qatar Airways are maintaining substantially more normal operations, providing improved access to the region, and restoring a good deal of the capacity lost during the initial disruption earlier this year. There have been signs of stability in Asia-Europe rates of late. OK, they’re more than 10% higher year on year at the moment, but well short of the levels we saw earlier this year.
“However, escalation in hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis, and renewed concerns over a resumption of the US-Iran war, mean Gulf carriers are again wondering what lies around the corner.”

Kia is crushing it with a full lineup of electric vehicles ranging from entry-level SUVs to the three-row EV9 and PV5 van. A leaked document revealed that Kia plans to add the EV7, a new midsize electric SUV, to fill the gap between the EV6 and the three-row EV9.
Kia EV7 is coming as a new midsize electric SUV
With 291,219 vehicles sold last month , up 10.3% from October 2025, Kia posted its eighth consecutive month of year-over-year sales growth.
Kia said it plans to build on the momentum by focusing on electrified vehicles in key markets, including hybrids in the US and fully electric vehicles in Europe.
After launching the EV2 earlier this year, Kia now offers one of the most complete EV lineups, including the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, and PV5 van.

According to a recently leaked document, a new midsize electric SUV will join the lineup. KoreanCarBlog uncovered an internal document from Kia’s Employment Stability Committee that reveals the company’s upcoming production plans.
The report claims “production of mid-range electric SUV ‘EV7’ to proceed” at Kia’s Gwangju factory in South Korea.
From left to right: Kia EV2, EV3, EV5, and EV9 (Source: Kia UK)
Although no other details were revealed, the EV7 will be a midsize electric SUV, slotted between the EV6 and three-row EV9.
During its 2026 CEO Investor Day in April, Kia announced plans to expand its EV lineup to 14 models by 2030.
In Europe, Kia plans for EVs to account for 66% of sales by 2030, with a full lineup that includes the EV2, EV3, EV4, EV5, EV6, EV9, three PBVs, a new C-segment electric SUV, and its first “SDV B-segment hatchback.”
Kia reveals plans to launch its first software-defined electric vehicle (Source: Kia)
So what can we expect from the upcoming EV7? Kia said earlier this year that it’s developing a new EV platform “to significantly enhance both product performance and cost competitiveness.”
Although it didn’t offer specifics, Kia claimed the new EV platform delivers up to a 40% increase in battery capacity and a 9% improvement in motor output.
It will use Kia’s fifth-generation batteries, providing up to 15% higher energy density than its current tech.
Kia’s upcoming software-defined vehicles (SDVs) are expected to integrate Hyundai’s SDV architecture (CODA), Pleos Connect infotainment system, and Gleo AI, an in-vehicle Agenic AI.They will also have Level 2++ autonomous driving capabilities on highways.
The EV5 , Kia’s current midsize electric SUV, is 4,615 mm long, 1,875 mm wide, and 1,675 mm tall, with a 2,750 mm wheelbase, which is about the size of the Sportage, so you can expect the EV7 to be slightly bigger. It will likely be closer in size to the Sorento.
Powered by an 81.4 kWh battery, the Kia’s current EV5 offers a WLTP range of up to 329 miles (530 km).
Kia EV5 (Source: Kia)
However, unlike the EV6 and EV9, the EV5 uses a 400V electrical architecture rather than an 800V. As a result, charging the battery from 10% to 80% takes about 30 minutes, rather than 18 to 25 minutes. The upcoming EV7 will likely use the 800V system for faster charging.
The document also revealed Kia will begin production of “completely redesigned models” at its Gwangmyeong Factory, including the 2028 Carnival Hybrid and a hydrogen-powered Carnival by 2029.
At its Gyeonggi Hwaseong Factory, Kia will reportedly also produce redesigned models, including the Sorento Hybrid in 2028.

This BMW M5 Competition Just Sold for $16,000 – No Catch Here
15 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
And we really mean it, there is no catch here, because as you can clearly see from the images shared below, it is the F10-generation of the BMW M5 , and some say it is the last true M5, because it was the final one to be offered strictly with rear-wheel drive.
As you likely recall, the F90 was all-wheel drive, and so is the modern-day G9X (G90 Sedan / G99 Touring). The F10 was made between 2011 and 2016, featuring a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission mated to the familiar 4.4-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine. The US and Canada also got a six-speed manual transmission option, but the car shown above does not have it.
The vehicle in question is a 2014 model year BMW M5 equipped with the Competition Package. Therefore, it has more oomph, enjoying 575 horsepower (583 ps/423 kW) and 502 pound-feet (680 Nm) of torque. As you already know, everything is channeled to the rear wheels, because the rear-biased xDrive all-wheel drive system was not available for this generation of the premium mid-size sedan.
The Competition Package boosted the output by 15 hp (15 ps/11 kW ), shaving one-tenth of a second from the 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) sprint compared to the standard M5 of that era, and 0.2 seconds when it came to the 0 to 124 mph (0-200 kph) acceleration. From 0-62 mph, the model needed a hair over the 4-second mark, though independent testing showed that it was some half a second faster than advertised.
Flat-out, it could do 155 mph (250 kph), though if you ticked the M Driver’s Package box on the options list, then the top speed would have increased to 190 mph (305 kph).
Photo: Cars&Bids This BMW M5 boasts the Competition Package, as we already told you, and also features the Executive Package and the Driver Assistance Package. It rides on the 343M wheels, which measure 20 inches in diameter, benefits from adaptive LED headlights, has Merino leather upholstery, a power sunroof, and a premium sound system from Bang & Olufsen.
Unfortunately, it also has some modifications, though it’s nothing that cannot be easily reverted back to the OEM configuration if the new owner does not fancy them, because these included the painted front reflectors, and the black kidney grilles.
But what about the known flaws, you ask? Well, this BMW M5 has some wear on the seats and interior surfaces, as you can see in the images shared in the gallery, as well as curb rash on the wheels. There are also some chips and scratches on the outside, and paint damage on the front bumper.
According to the seller, who reportedly bought this machine in July 2026, adding some 5,000 miles (~8,000 km), the car “ drives very good, ” and the “ last owner took good care of it. ” At the time of cataloging, this ride had 118,500 miles (190,700 km) on the clock, so it is a high-mileage example.
The current market value of a high-mileage BMW M5 from the 2014 model year is between $20,000 and $25,000, though vehicles with over 90,000 miles (145,000 km) in rough usually change hands for roughly $20,000. Vehicles in good condition with some 50,000 to 80,000 miles (80,000-129,000 km) usually go from $26,000 to $35,000, and low-mileage machines with less than 40,000 miles (~65,000 km) can cost close to $50,000.
Photo: Cars&Bids It is worth noting that the Competition Package models usually fetch a $3,000 to $5,000 premium in today’s used car market in the United States of America. Therefore, in theory, this particular 2014 BMW M5 Competition should have gone for around $25,000. However, it fetched a lot less, because as we already told you in the title, it went for $16,000.
The business super sedan , which has a Singapore Gray Metallic paint finish on the outside and a black interior, was advertised on Cars&Bids as part of an online auction that ended on November 3, 2026. The car failed to sell when the gavel hit the table, but it changed hands shortly after for the aforementioned sum.
It has a clean Arizona title, a clean Carfax history report showing that it has no mileage discrepancies and has never been involved in an accident, and has been registered mostly in California since it left the dealership back in the day. Besides the car, the next owner will get a spare set of floor mats, and one key, the listing reveals.
Now, paying $16K for a great business super sedan is definitely a win, in my book anyway, because this is a lot of car for the money, so congrats to the new owner. But if you came across this F10 BMW M5 Competition listed for $16K, would you have bought it? Before clicking on this link , which will take you to the ad, feel free to speak your mind about it in the comments area below.

Yamaha NMAX Scooters Are Going Electric, 65-Mile Range Is on the Table with the E
45 photos
Photo: Yamaha
The scooter market is very profitable for those in this line of work these days, and that is pretty obvious just by looking at how many of them there are out there. Some are better at the job than others, but if you ask me, at least over in Europe, one scooter-making company reigns supreme: Yamaha.
The Japanese company has plenty of models on the table in this segment, but they still don't seem to be enough to satisfy people's appetite for Yamaha scooters. Especially when talking about the ones in the Max family, a go-to choice for many buyers over the past two and a half decades.
The range is a pretty solid one already, but up until this week, the week of the 2026 Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA), it didn't offer any version powered by an electric drivetrain. Well, now it does.
Enter the Yamaha NMAX E Sport Scooter, a newcomer to the range built on a brand-new platform tailored for an electric powertrain and designed to help the bike maker fulfill its commitment to a green future.
In more ways than one, the new two-wheeler is the same as the others in the range, but it opens up an entirely new segment for the company, one that could prove very lucrative in the troubled days we live through.
The NMAX E plays in the 125cc class, but it does so with a 3,5 kWh lithium-ion battery and a ten horsepower/ 33 Nm of torque clutchless permanent magnet synchronous motor that can spin at a maximum of 3,500 rpm.
The hardware has been designed to offer a maximum range of 64 miles (104 km), which is more than enough for daily commutes in crowded cities. Charging, though, could prove a bit of a challenge, as the small battery pack needs up to 5.5 hours to get from zero to 100 percent using the onboard 800W charger.
All of the fittings customers make use of on all the other Max scooters can be found on the E as well, including the three ride modes and the reverse function, the five-inch TFT display with smartphone connectivity, and the long dual seat.
Yamaha will roll out the new scooter model in the spring of next year, but, at least for now, it doesn't offer any info on price. We do know the two-wheeler will premiere two new color schemes, Avio Blue and Platinum Silver.
Taking advantage of the launch of the electric scooter, Yamaha has also birthed something called the YOU Charge, which it describes as a solution for quick and convenient access to public charging. The details on that are quite scarce at the moment, but we'll get back to that as soon as we know more.
